title.rendered: Reigning in Life Through Christ: The Gospel For Today

content.rendered:
Those who receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness will reign in life through the One, Jesus Christ. Reign. Not endure. Not survive. Reign. This is the New Testament’s description of the ordinary Christian life.

The Gospel For Today | Sunday, August 2, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“For if by the one man’s offense death reigned through the one, much more those who receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness will reign in life through the One, Jesus Christ.”
Romans 5:17 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Paul is contrasting two Adams. The first Adam, through whose disobedience death entered the human story. The second Adam, Jesus Christ, through whose obedience life comes to the human story. Under the first Adam, death reigned over humanity. Under the second Adam, believers now reign in life over what once reigned over them. This is one of the most extraordinary statements in the New Testament about who the believer has become in Christ.

The Passion Translation opens up the depth of the promise: “Death once held us in its grip, and by the blunder of one man, death reigned as king over humanity. But now, how much more are we held in the grip of grace and continue reigning as kings in life, empowered by the gift of perfect righteousness through the one and only Jesus, the Anointed One” (Romans 5:17 TPT). Continuing reigning as kings in life. That is the language Paul reaches for.

The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “For if because of one man’s trespass (lapse, offense) death reigned through that one, much more surely will those who receive [God’s] overflowing grace (unmerited favor) and the free gift of righteousness [putting them into right standing with Himself] reign as kings in life through the one Man Jesus Christ (the Messiah, the Anointed One)” (Romans 5:17 AMPC).

Two words Paul uses matter enormously. Abundance and reign. Abundance of grace. Not measured, careful grace. Overflowing, super-abounding grace. And what does the recipient of that abundance do? They reign in life. The Greek word is basileusousin, from the same root as basileus, king. The believer, having received abundance of grace and the gift of righteousness, now operates in the position of a king in daily life. Not as an abstract theological idea. As the actual, daily posture of the redeemed.

What does reigning in life look like? It means that life circumstances do not have the final word over the believer. Sickness may knock, but health reigns because of Christ. Fear may whisper, but courage reigns because of Christ. Poverty may threaten, but provision reigns because of Christ. Death may terrify others, but resurrection reigns for the believer because of Christ. The believer is no longer a subject of what used to reign over them. They are, through the abundance of grace, reigning in life through the One Jesus Christ.

For Gospelbuzz readers, today is Sunday. In churches across the world, believers will worship a King. The truth Paul unfolds in Romans 5:17 is that the same believers, worshipping the King, are being called to reign as kings under Him in ordinary life. Not passively. Not defeated. Not intimidated. Reigning through the abundance of grace and the gift of righteousness. Walk in that posture today.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that I reign in life through the One, Jesus Christ. I have received the abundance of Your grace and the gift of righteousness that puts me in right standing with You. I am no longer a subject of what used to reign over my life. Sickness does not reign. Fear does not reign. Poverty does not reign. Death does not reign. Christ reigns, and in Him, through the abundance of grace, I reign in life. I walk in that royal posture today, humble under the King, and reigning through Him. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I reign in life through the One, Jesus Christ. The abundance of grace and the gift of righteousness are mine in Him. I walk as a royal, humble under the King, reigning through Him.
